feed.title: Daily Data Lab
feed.subtitle: One small interactive data visualization a day, built with React and public data.

entry.title: Day 011: Who grows and buys the world's spices, how concentrated is supply, and how does today's map compare with the old Spice Route?
entry.summary: Production and trade of eight FAOSTAT spice groups in every country since 1961, the 50 largest trade flows of each, how concentrated supply is, what a kilogram is worth, and eight cited moments of the historic Spice Route, with black pepper and Mexico's vanilla up close.

entry.title: Day 010: How many people have lost the night sky, how fast are the stars fading, and where are dark skies protected?
entry.summary: The share of people and land under light-polluted skies in every country, from the 2015 world atlas of artificial sky brightness, next to fifteen years of citizen-science star counts, the gap between what satellites and human eyes measure, and where certified dark-sky places are, with a close-up of Arizona and Sonora.

entry.title: Day 009: Where do people live longest and healthiest, and do blue zones survive age validation?
entry.summary: Life expectancy and healthy life expectancy for every country, with WHO's uncertainty intervals, the years lived in less than full health, centenarians, the female advantage and the Preston curve, next to what the blue-zone studies actually measured and the scientific debate over whether their ages are real.

entry.title: Day 008: How much crop diversity is safeguarded, and how much is backed up in Svalbard?
entry.summary: All 1.42 million seed samples in the Svalbard Global Seed Vault, by depositor, crop, and year, set against the 6 million accessions that the world's genebanks report to FAO, with how concentrated the backup is and how much of each country's collection it covers.

entry.title: Day 007: How much of Earth orbit is junk, and who left it there?
entry.summary: Every object in CelesTrak's satellite catalogue, 71,000 since 1957, sorted into working satellites, dead ones, rocket bodies, and fragments, by orbit, altitude, year, and owner, set against ESA's estimate of more than 1.5 million pieces too small to track.

entry.title: Day 006: Where is the world's food wasted, and by whom?
entry.summary: UNEP's 1.05 billion tonnes of food wasted in 2022, split into homes, restaurants, and shops for all 228 countries, set against hunger, income, and climate, with Mexico and the United States side by side.

entry.title: Day 005: Which languages are endangered and barely documented?
entry.summary: All 7,685 spoken first languages in Glottolog 5.4, mapped by how endangered they are and how well they are described, with the families and countries most at risk and the gaps in the world's grammar databases.

entry.title: Day 004: How fast are winters warming at Abraham Lake?
entry.summary: The Alberta reservoir famous for methane bubbles frozen in its ice, set against 1.43 million lakes in HydroLAKES and 75 winters of ERA5 air temperature, with the warming trend of the world's largest lakes, growing every day.

entry.title: Day 003: Where and when do light pillars appear?
entry.summary: An atlas of photographed light pillars, sun dogs, and ice halos from 2000 to 2026, with the weather at each moment and a 3-D simulator of the ice crystals that turn a light into a column.

entry.title: Day 002: Where do New Zealand's glowworms shine?
entry.summary: Every public record of the Waitomo glowworm on a night-sky map of New Zealand, set against the weather outside the caves where the larvae light up the ceilings.

entry.title: Day 001: When is the best time to cross from Mexicali?
entry.summary: Live and historical wait times at the Calexico ports of entry, with the best and worst hours to cross by day of the week.
